name.text: Calculating exact value of sine theta

questiontext.text:

Find the exact value of \(\sin\theta\).

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution

The point \(P = (\cos\theta,\, \sin\theta)\) lies on the unit circle, so it is at distance \(1\) from \(O\). By Pythagoras' theorem this gives the identity

\[ \sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1. \]

The identity gives the size of \(\sin\theta\); the quadrant gives its sign.

Step 1: make \(\sin^2\theta\) the subject.

\[ \sin^2\theta = 1 - \cos^2\theta. \]

Step 2: substitute \(\cos\theta = {@cos_value@}\). Squaring a negative number gives a positive result, so the sign of \(\cos\theta\) does not matter here:

\[ \sin^2\theta = 1 - \left({@cos_value@}\right)^2 = 1 - {@cos_abs^2@} = {@sin_abs^2@}. \]

Step 3: take the square root. Every positive number has two square roots:

\[ \sin\theta = \pm\sqrt{ {@sin_abs^2@} } = \pm {@sin_abs@}. \]

Step 4: use the quadrant to choose the sign. \(\sin\theta\) is the \(y\)-coordinate of \(P\). In Quadrant {@quadname@}, \(P\) is [[if test="is(quadrant=2)"]]above the \(x\)-axis, so \(\sin\theta\) is positive[[else]]below the \(x\)-axis, so \(\sin\theta\) is negative[[/if]]. Therefore

\[ \sin\theta = {@ta@}. \]

Check. \(\left({@ta@}\right)^2 + \left({@cos_value@}\right)^2 = {@sin_abs^2@} + {@cos_abs^2@} = 1\). The diagram shows the right-angled triangle with hypotenuse \(1\), horizontal side \({@cos_abs@}\) and vertical side \({@sin_abs@}\).

truefeedback.text: Your answer has the same size as \(\cos\theta\). \(\sin\theta\) and \(\cos\theta\) are different here. Use the identity \(\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1\) to find the size of \(\sin\theta\).

node.description: Forgot to take the square root

truefeedback.text: Your answer looks like the value of \(\sin^2\theta\). You still need to take the square root to find \(\sin\theta\).

falsefeedback.text: Use the identity \(\sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta = 1\): make \(\sin^2\theta\) the subject, substitute the value of \(\cos\theta\) and take the square root. Then use the quadrant to choose the sign.
